summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every video gets roughly 700-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best performers use a 'X doesn't see/hear, it only senses Y' hook, robots and clap switches, and the oldest videos on YouTube (Oct 29-Nov 5) got the most views there. Plain question titles like 'How does X work?' about public-place gadgets (taps, lifts, doors, smoke alarms) and the English video do poorly, and several videos never reached Instagram at all.
winningPattern: Hindi, surprising 'doesn't X, only Y' statements about a relatable sensor-based thing (robot, clap switch, mic, DHT11 heat sensor), with an emoji and #shorts, posted mainly on Instagram. Robots and sound-triggered gadgets get the most saves and shares; the title gives a myth-busting twist, not a plain question.
doMore: Make robot and clap-switch style demos: show the gadget failing or reacting in a surprising way, with a visible result
Use the 'Ye X nahi, sirf Y' contrast hook in the first line on screen
Post every video on Instagram too, since YouTube-only videos get no Instagram reach
Make follow-ups or part 2s of the top videos (gyro robot, clap switch, IR robot) and the shareable ones
End with a prompt to save or share (e.g. 'Kisi maker dost ko bhejo') to boost saves and shares
stopDoing: Plain 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' titles on everyday public gadgets like taps, lifts and malls doors
Posting near-duplicate topics (three clap switch, four IR/PIR, two smoke videos) in the same month
Posting English or YouTube-only videos until the Hindi Instagram formula is steady
